concepts.def: Region around a magnet/current where a magnetic material feels a force; lines run N→S.
Permanent keeps its magnetism; induced is magnetic only in a field.
A coil carrying a current; stronger with more turns, current or an iron core.
A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a force (Fleming's left hand).
Moving a wire through a field induces a potential difference.
Changes the size of an alternating voltage using two coils on an iron core.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnetism & Electromagnetism — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Magnetism & Electromagnetism brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Magnetism & Electromagnetism.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s². What is the resultant force?
options: 2 N
8 N
6 N

mcqs.q: What does it mean if the resultant force on an object is zero?
options: The object must be stationary.
The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
The object is decelerating.
The object is accelerating.

mcqs.q: Why are infrared cameras used to detect warm objects in the dark?
options: Infrared cameras shine infrared light onto objects so they reflect back visibly.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
Warm objects emit infrared radiation due to their temperature; the camera detects this emission.

mcqs.q: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Is it accelerating?
options: No — constant speed means no acceleration.
Only if it speeds up or slows down on the circle.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Yes — its direction is constantly changing, so its velocity changes; centripetal acceleration points toward the centre of the circle.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the activity of a source and the dose received by a person?
options: Activity (Bq) is the rate of nuclear decays in the source; dose (Sv) measures the biological effect of absorbed radiation on tissue.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
Activity and dose are the same — both measure how dangerous the radiation is.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Force”?
options: The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).
The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Weight”?
options: The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
A diagram showing all forces acting on a single object as arrows from its centre.
The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).

options: Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
